Goal: I can explain why side ratios in right triangles depend only on the angle.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Any two right triangles with the same acute angle θ are similar by AA (the right angles and θ match). So the ratios of their sides are equal, no matter how big the triangles are.

That means each ratio, such as opposite leg over adjacent leg, depends only on the angle. For 35 degrees, opposite over adjacent is about 0.700 in every right triangle. These fixed ratios are the trigonometric ratios.
